# `traffic`

Group: **Traffic**. What moves and what transmits: the fleet, its size, roadside units and the backend.

70 settings. The status column says whether editing a setting changes a run; see [how to read these tables](../overview.md). Paths use `[]` for a list element and `*` for a map key.

|---|---|
| :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } | `wired` |
| :material-circle-half-full:{ title="Partly active" } | `partial` |

How big a gap in the main-road traffic drivers wait for before pulling out at a junction without lights, or turning right on red where that is allowed: below 1 they squeeze in, above 1 they wait longer. |

| <span id="s-traffic-lc-keep-right"></span>`traffic.lc_keep_right` | number | | | [0, 10]<br>recommended Unset (today's MOBIL); 1 (SUMO default); 0 to 2. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | LC2013's eagerness to move back right when the right lane is free (0 off). Unset is off. Whether trucks and buses, which accelerate slowly, wait for longer gaps in traffic than cars before pulling out or turning left across it. |
| <span id="s-traffic-critical-gap-cv"></span>`traffic.critical_gap_cv` | number | | | [0, 0.5]<br>recommended 0 (today); 0.18 for realistic drivers (field spreads 0.15 to 0.2). | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | The spread of drivers' critical gaps: each driver's is lognormal around the HCM value with this coefficient of variation (0.15-0.2 in field studies, SUMO P1; 0.18 is the realistic preset), at unsignalised junctions, on a permitted left and on a right turn on red. | <span id="s-traffic-time-to-impatience-s"></span>`traffic.time_to_impatience_s` | number | s | | [0, 3600]<br>recommended 0 (off, today); 180 s (SUMO) for realistic waiting. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | Seconds of standing after which a yielding driver's impatience is full and its critical gap has fallen to `impatience_gap_floor` of its own (SUMO `--time-to-impatience`, 180 s). Unset is 0: no impatience. How long a driver waiting to pull out or turn across traffic stands before they accept the shortest gap they ever will; the longer they wait, the smaller the gap they take. |
| <span id="s-traffic-impatience-gap-floor"></span>`traffic.impatience_gap_floor` | number | | | [0.3, 1]<br>recommended 0.7; 0.5 to 0.9. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | The critical gap at full impatience as a share of the driver's own. Unset is 0.7. How short a gap a driver who has waited a long time accepts, as a share of the gap they wanted at first. |
| <span id="s-traffic-impatience-foe-braking"></span>`traffic.impatience_foe_braking` | boolean | | | recommended Off; on for SUMO-like assertive drivers. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | Whether an impatient driver judges an approaching foe as if it would brake at impatience times 4.5 m/s² (SUMO's blend toward the foe's braking arrival). Unset is off. Whether an impatient driver pulls out counting on oncoming cars to brake for them. |
| <span id="s-traffic-permissive-sneakers"></span>`traffic.permissive_sneakers` | integer | vehicles per lane per cycle | | [0, 4]<br>recommended 0 (today); 2 (HCM) for realistic left turns. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | How many permitted left turners per lane may complete the turn in the amber that ends a permissive green, the HCM's "sneakers" (2 per cycle). Each must cross the stop line before the red. Unset is 0: none. How many drivers waiting to turn left on a green may finish the turn as the light turns yellow, when oncoming traffic stops; without them a left turn into steady oncoming traffic can wait for minutes. |
| <span id="s-traffic-standing-leader-stop"></span>`traffic.standing_leader_stop` | boolean | | | recommended Off (today); on for smooth stops behind queues (the realistic benchmark sets it). | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | Whether a driver closing on a standing vehicle brakes at no less than the constant deceleration that stops it at its standstill gap, as at a stop line, instead of being stopped in one step when the car-following model's braking (which scales with its acceleration, low for vans and trucks) arrives too late. Unset is off. Whether drivers coming up behind a stopped car brake smoothly to stop at their usual gap, as they do at a stop line, rather than braking late and stopping abruptly (vans and trucks, whose following model brakes gently, were stopped in one step). |
| <span id="s-traffic-depart-speed-max"></span>`traffic.depart_speed_max` | boolean | | | recommended Off (today, SUMO's default); on for freeways and other roads entered at speed (SUMO departSpeed=max). | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | Whether a trip enters the road already moving, at the highest safe speed there (SUMO's `departSpeed="max"`) instead of at rest (SUMO's default, `departSpeed="0"`): a freeway entry merges at speed. Unset is off. Whether cars enter the road already moving, at the fastest speed that is safe there, as traffic joining a freeway does, rather than appearing parked in the lane and pulling away from rest. |
| <span id="s-traffic-lane-bend-speed"></span>`traffic.lane_bend_speed` | boolean | | | recommended Off (today); on with turn_curve_window_m 6 for kinked city streets (the realistic benchmark sets it). | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | Whether the bends of a through lane's polyline are driven no faster than the turn-speed rule allows (`turn_lateral_accel_mps2` over the tightest `turn_curve_window_m`, 6 m when unset), as a junction connector is. Unset is off. Whether drivers slow for sharp bends in a street's mapped centreline as they do for corners at junctions; without it a car follows a kink in the map at full speed. |
| <span id="s-traffic-depart-at-speed"></span>`traffic.depart_at_speed` | boolean | | | recommended Off (today); on for realistic map edges (no false halts or stopped-vehicle warnings there). | basic | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | Whether a vehicle entering the map from outside it (its origin a lane no road of the map feeds, at the map's edge) is put on at the start of that lane at its desired speed, capped by the speed that is safe behind the vehicle ahead and that can still stop at the lane's end, as SUMO's departSpeed="desired" with departPos="base" does. Origins inside the network stay at rest. Unset is off. Whether cars entering the map from outside it are already moving, as real traffic crossing the map's edge is, instead of starting from rest at the edge; cars starting inside the map still start from rest. |
| <span id="s-traffic-reroute-share"></span>`traffic.reroute_share` | number | | | [0, 1]<br>recommended 1 (every driver, today); about 0.3-0.6 for today's navigation-app use in a US city. | basic | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | The share of drivers who re-route on information, 0-1, drawn once per driver (SUMO device.rerouting.probability). The rest keep the route they chose and detour only round a closure they can see. Unset is 1: every driver. The share of drivers who change route on information (a navigation app or a received V2X warning); the rest keep the route they chose and only detour round a closure they can see. |
| <span id="s-traffic-reroute-source"></span>`traffic.reroute_source` | json (v2xw_mobility::routing::dynamic::RerouteSource) | | | recommended navigation (today); v2x to measure what V2X hazard warnings are worth to routing. | basic | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | Where those drivers learn that the road has changed: `navigation` (a navigation app: network-wide, on speeds smoothed over three minutes, and every closure) or `v2x` (only a DENM or TIM their own unit received and verified, placing a blocking event on their route: local and belief-only). Unset is navigation. Where re-routing drivers learn that the road has changed: a navigation app, which sees the whole network a few minutes late, or only the V2X hazard warnings their own car received, which are local and immediate. |

| <span id="s-traffic-signals-control"></span>`traffic.signals.control` | string | | | `fixed-time`, `actuated`, `nema`<br>recommended fixed-time for a repeatable baseline; actuated to study signal timing or SPaT that changes; nema for US controller behaviour (FHWA Signal Timing Manual 2nd ed.). | basic | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | Fixed-time, single-ring vehicle-actuated, or the NEMA dual ring. How the traffic lights decide when to change: on a fixed clock, or actuated by detectors in the road that hold a green while cars keep coming and end it early when the street goes quiet, as most US suburban and many city signals do. nema runs the US eight-phase dual-ring controller: both directions' throughs and lefts time side by side, with pedestrian push buttons, left-turn arrows, coordination and emergency-vehicle priority. |

## kerbside

| Setting | Type | Unit | Default | Range or choices | Level | Status | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| <span id="s-traffic-kerbside-enabled"></span>`traffic.kerbside.enabled` | boolean | | | recommended On for city realism; off for a clean baseline. | basic | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | Whether vehicles stop at the kerb at all. Unset is on. Whether buses stop at stops, taxis pick up and delivery vans double-park, briefly blocking a lane as they do in a real city. |
| <span id="s-traffic-kerbside-bus-stop-spacing-m"></span>`traffic.kerbside.bus_stop_spacing_m` | number | m | | [100, 2000]<br>recommended 200 to 400 m for local buses. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | The distance from one bus stop to the next along a bus's route, metres. Unset is 260 m. How far apart bus stops are along a bus route. |
| <span id="s-traffic-kerbside-bus-dwell-mean-s"></span>`traffic.kerbside.bus_dwell_mean_s` | number | s | | [5, 300]<br>recommended 15 to 60 s (TCQSM). | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | The mean time a bus stands at a stop, seconds. Unset is 60 s. How long a bus stands at each stop on average. |
| <span id="s-traffic-kerbside-taxi-share"></span>`traffic.kerbside.taxi_share` | number | | | [0, 1]<br>recommended 0 outside a downtown; 0.2 to 0.3 in Midtown Manhattan. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | The share of passenger cars that are taxis or for-hire cars and stop at the kerb once on their trip. Unset is the jurisdiction's (0, or 0.3 in Midtown Manhattan). The share of cars that are taxis or ride-hail cars making one kerbside stop. |
| <span id="s-traffic-kerbside-taxi-dwell-median-s"></span>`traffic.kerbside.taxi_dwell_median_s` | number | s | | [5, 600]<br>recommended 20 to 60 s. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | The median time a taxi stands at the kerb, seconds. Unset is 30 s. How long a taxi stands at the kerb for a pick-up or drop-off. |
| <span id="s-traffic-kerbside-delivery-stop-share"></span>`traffic.kerbside.delivery_stop_share` | number | | | [0, 1]<br>recommended 0.3 to 0.6. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | The share of delivery vans and trucks that make one delivery stop on their trip. Unset is 0.6. The share of vans and trucks that stop once on their trip to deliver. |
| <span id="s-traffic-kerbside-delivery-dwell-median-s"></span>`traffic.kerbside.delivery_dwell_median_s` | number | s | | [30, 3600]<br>recommended 5 to 15 minutes. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | The median time a delivery stop lasts, seconds. Unset is 600 s. How long a delivery stop lasts. |

## vehicle_dynamics

| Setting | Type | Unit | Default | Range or choices | Level | Status | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| <span id="s-traffic-vehicle-dynamics-grade"></span>`traffic.vehicle_dynamics.grade` | boolean | | | recommended Off (today); on for hilly maps (SUMO's KraussPS slope term). | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | The slope term: a vehicle's acceleration less g times the sine of the road's grade, as SUMO's KraussPS has it. Unset is off. Whether hills slow vehicles down: on a climb a driver gets less acceleration from the same pedal, and on a descent the car holds its speed. Needs a map with terrain heights; flat maps are unchanged. |
| <span id="s-traffic-vehicle-dynamics-power-limit"></span>`traffic.vehicle_dynamics.power_limit` | boolean | | | recommended Off (today); on with grade for hilly maps and freight corridors. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | The power term: no more acceleration than the engine's power gives after rolling and air resistance, for the classes with a sourced road-load row (passenger car, tractor-trailer, rigid truck, bus, coach and van). Unset is off. Whether an engine's power limits how fast a vehicle can speed up, so a loaded tractor-trailer crawls up a long climb at about 46 km/h on a 5% grade while a car keeps the limit. Applies to cars, tractor-trailers, rigid trucks, buses, coaches and vans, from cited figures (FTA bus tests, EPA road loads, NCHRP 505); motorcycles have none yet. |

## emergency_yield

| Setting | Type | Unit | Default | Range or choices | Level | Status | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| <span id="s-traffic-emergency-yield-enabled"></span>`traffic.emergency_yield.enabled` | boolean | | | recommended Off (today); on for emergency-vehicle studies, where travel time through traffic is the point. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | Whether drivers yield at all. Unset is off. Whether drivers get out of the way of an ambulance, fire engine or police car running its lights and siren: in the US they move to the right-hand lane and stop, clear of the junction, until it has passed (NY VTL 1144(a)). Off, an emergency vehicle has to queue like everyone else. |
| <span id="s-traffic-emergency-yield-reaction-distance-m"></span>`traffic.emergency_yield.reaction_distance_m` | number | m | | [1, 500]<br>recommended 25 m (SUMO's bluelight default); more on a quiet street where a siren carries, less in heavy traffic. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | How far behind a driver an emergency vehicle with its siren on is noticed, metres (gap from its front bumper to the driver's rear). Unset is 25 m, SUMO's bluelight device `reactiondist` default. How far behind a driver an emergency vehicle is when they notice it and start to pull over. |
| <span id="s-traffic-emergency-yield-red-pass-speed-mps"></span>`traffic.emergency_yield.red_pass_speed_mps` | number | m/s | | [0, 10]<br>recommended 0 (a full stop, the fire-service rule); 2 to 4 m/s for services that let their drivers roll through slowly. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | The speed an emergency vehicle slows to at a red before it passes on, once the junction is clear, m/s (UVC §11-106(b)2). Unset is 0: a full stop first, as fire-service practice has it. How slowly an ambulance or fire engine takes a red light it is allowed to pass: 0 means it stops first, then goes once the junction is clear. |

## Choices

The labelled values of every closed or model setting above.

??? note "`traffic.signals.control`"

 | Value | Label | Meaning |
 |---|---|---|
 | `fixed-time` | Fixed time | Every signal runs its plan's clock: each phase lasts its stated time, whatever the traffic. |
 | `actuated` | Actuated (single ring) | Detectors hold a green while cars keep arriving and end it early when the approach goes quiet, one phase at a time. |
 | `nema` | NEMA dual ring (eight phases) | Two rings of four phases time concurrently and meet at barriers, as US controllers do (FHWA Signal Timing Manual 2nd ed.), with protected, permissive or protected-then-permissive lefts. Junctions that do not map keep the single ring. |

??? note "`traffic.signals.detector_placement`"

 | Value | Label | Meaning |
 |---|---|---|
 | `stop-line` | Stop line | A presence loop covering the last `detector_m` of every approach lane (FHWA Signal Timing Manual 2e, ch. |
 | `sumo` | Sumo | SUMO's `actuated` default (MSActuatedTrafficLightLogic): one induction loop per approach lane, the lane's speed limit times `detector-gap` = 2 s upstream of the stop line (at least 1 m, at most the… |

??? note "`traffic.signals.nema.lefts`"

 | Value | Label | Meaning |
 |---|---|---|
 | `lead-lead` | Lead-lead | Both left turns go before their opposing throughs: the most common US sequence (FHWA STM 2nd ed. §5.1.3.6). |
 | `lag-lag` | Lag-lag | Both left turns go after their opposing throughs. |
 | `lead-lag` | Lead-lag | One left leads and the opposing left lags, which suits a green wave in both directions. |

??? note "`traffic.signals.nema.left_turn_mode`"

 | Value | Label | Meaning |
 |---|---|---|
 | `protected-permissive` | Protected, then permissive | A green arrow first, then lefts may turn through gaps in the oncoming traffic. |
 | `protected` | Protected only | Lefts turn only on their own green arrow (even from a lane shared with the through, which they then block). |
 | `permissive` | Permissive only | No left-turn phase: lefts turn through gaps in the oncoming traffic. |

??? note "`traffic.signals.nema.permissive_display`"

 | Value | Label | Meaning |
 |---|---|---|
 | `fya` | Flashing yellow arrow | The permissive left shows a flashing yellow arrow (MUTCD 2009 §4D.20). |
 | `green-ball` | Circular green | The permissive left shows the circular green of the through (MUTCD 2009 §4D.18). |

??? note "`traffic.signals.nema.force_off`"

 | Value | Label | Meaning |
 |---|---|---|
 | `floating` | Floating force-offs | Each side-street phase ends by its own split, so time it leaves goes to the coordinated main street. |
 | `fixed` | Fixed force-offs | Force-off points are fixed in the cycle, so a later phase may use time an earlier one left. |

??? note "`traffic.signals.nema.controller_type`"

 | Value | Label | Meaning |
 |---|---|---|
 | `ts2` | NEMA TS 2 | The coordination offset is measured to the start of the coordinated green. |
 | `type170` | Type 170 | The coordination offset is measured to the start of the coordinated yellow. |
